description: In this workshop, students read literary and scholarly texts about food and then produce their own
food writing. Topics may include food's relationship with intergenerationality, social movements,
travel, migration, conflict, and climate. During workshops, students apply journalistic principles
to draft restaurant reviews and feature stories (such as culinary travelogues or stories profiling
their own food traditions), use instructional theory to adapt found/family recipes, and craft
graphically rich, digital page spreads showcasing their food writing. Offered periodically.
